Chloe / Laura — quick tech notes I prepared to include in the package for OrionVR. I’ll attach the architecture diagram and the RBAC matrix. Key points:  

- Delegated SCIM provisioning: Redwood supports SCIM 2.0 for user and group provisioning. For delegated scenarios we support a customer-managed SCIM connector (runs in customer VPC or private connector) which exchanges a scoped service token with Redwood’s provisioning gateway. The connector model allows multiple downstream directories to be managed while keeping service account secrets customer-controlled.
  - Controls: short-lived service tokens (rotated automatically every 7 days), role-scoped tokens (least privilege), and optional HSM/KMS-backed key storage when deployed in Private mode.
  - Evidence to attach: scim-architecture-diagram.pdf, example token rotation entry from audit logs (included in runbook).

- SAML / attribute mapping: recommended assertion attribute mappings: email (urn:oid:0.9.2342.19200300.100.1.3), groups (urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Group), role (custom: urn:redwood:role). I’ll export a sample IdP metadata file and our SP metadata.

- MFA & role elevation: MFA is enforced for console admin users on all Dedicated and Private plans; for Hosted customers it is enforced for admin-level accounts by policy and we recommend requiring MFA via IdP (IdP-enforced MFA). Service account creation and role elevation flows are guarded: elevation events require owner approval and produce an audit log entry with the elevation reason.

I attached RBAC matrix (rbac-matrix-v1.csv) and a draft of the SSO runbook (sso-runbook-v1.2.pdf). I’ll also capture screenshots of the console policy page (mfa-policy-screenshot.png) and export the SAML metadata (redwood-sso-metadata.xml).

Notes on redaction: we will redact internal hostnames and customer-specific identifiers from the artifacts.

-Rafael
